item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00231","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C04","C01","C19"],"selected_candidate_label":"C04","confidence":0.84,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C04 provides the strongest reusable template because both memoranda reject private bills that would waive a limitations period and confer Court of Claims jurisdiction over stale claims. They follow a materially parallel structure: describe that machinery, recount the claimants' failure to act timely, defend limitations as necessary to orderly administration, and reject exceptional treatment because comparable claimants would remain barred. C01 and C19 contain closer snippets about an unexplained failure to file timely and discrimination against similarly situated claimants, but their tax-refund setting supplies less of the child's specific legal machinery.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The bill would waive the applicable statute of limitations and confer jurisdiction upon the Court of Claims to hear the claims","parent_excerpt":"The bill (H. R. 9950) provides that, notwithstanding any statute of limitations or lapse of time, jurisdiction is conferred upon the Court of Claims to hear, determine, and render judgment upon the claims","explanation":"This is substantially the same operative legislative mechanism, adapted from federal employees' compensation claims to Philippine wartime property claims."},{"child_excerpt":"these claimants had ample opportunity to present their claims in a timely manner","parent_excerpt":"The claims were not asserted in timely fashion by the claimants","explanation":"Both memoranda make the claimants' delinquency central to the disapproval."},{"child_excerpt":"Nothing in the record justifies special treatment for these claimants, particularly when it is remembered that many others filed suit against the United States in the Court of Claims ... and had their cases dismissed because of the expiration of the statute of limitations.","parent_excerpt":"If I were to approve this bill, I could not in all fairness refuse to approve other bills setting aside the statute of limitations on old claims","explanation":"Both conclude that waiving limitations for the named claimants would unfairly privilege them over other stale claimants."}]}
